summary: Failed-login lockout to blunt brute-force / credential-stuffing against the standalone local-user login. New apis.LoginGuard (in-memory, thread-safe), keyed per source IP, wired into NewLocalBasicAuth: after maxAttempts failures within windowSeconds the IP is locked, with the lockout doubling on each repeat up to lockoutMaxSeconds (escalating backoff). A small per-failure delay slows online guessing; locked requests return 429 + Retry-After (whole seconds, also echoed in the JSON body as retryAfterSeconds) with a generic message that never reveals whether the username or password was wrong. The login page shows a live countdown and disables the form until it expires. A lockout trip publishes a Critical system notification (NotifyAuthLockout) that fans out to webhook/Telegram/MQTT destinations. New config block loginSecurity in config.json + AppConfigModel.LoginSecurity (enabled, maxAttempts=5, windowSeconds=300, lockoutSeconds=60, lockoutMaxSeconds=900, failedDelayMs=500, notifyOnLockout=true).
compatibility: Backward compatible; defaults are conservative and only affect repeated failed logins. Keying is per-IP, so a locked IP also blocks valid-cookie sessions from that same IP during an active attack (matters on shared-IP/NAT). State is in-memory and resets on restart. Disable by setting loginSecurity.enabled=false.
